items.text: All 4 round-1 decisions have been resolved and incorporated into the plan: WebSocket transport (not SSE), action registry pattern, WS connect only on Operations lens, inline error UX. Contract Decisions section is now populated. The plan has been updated with detailed Node ID formats, existing API endpoints, WS message types, and phased implementation strategy.

items.topic: Navigation actions: where do 'View Logs', 'View Prompt Trace', 'View Execution History' navigate?
items.context: Several inspector actions are navigation-based rather than API calls. We need to decide where they go. The swarm-manager UI has existing pages: BacklogDetailsPage (at /backlog/{kind}/{name}), ScenarioDetailsPage (at /scenarios/{name}). Execution records and prompt traces may not have dedicated pages yet. Options for rendering this content without new pages.

options.label: Navigate to existing detail pages where they exist; for missing pages, open a modal/drawer with the content
options.rationale: Uses what exists (BacklogDetailsPage, ScenarioDetailsPage) for navigation. For execution details and prompt traces that lack a dedicated page, render a modal or drawer in the graph workspace itself. Avoids creating new routes. Recommended because it keeps users in the graph context for operational data while leveraging existing pages for detail views.

options.label: All navigation actions open the existing detail pages (create new pages for execution/prompt trace if needed)
options.rationale: Consistent pattern: every 'View X' navigates away. But requires creating ExecutionDetailsPage and PromptTracePage which is out of scope for this item.

options.label: All navigation actions expand an enlarged Inspector panel (no page navigation at all)
options.rationale: Keeps user in graph context always. But the Inspector would need to become much more complex, essentially embedding full detail views.

items.context: When a node receives a WebSocket update on the Operations lens, it should show a brief visual indicator. The question is how prominent this should be and how to implement it without re-rendering the entire graph.

options.label: CSS-only ring pulse animation (2s fade) triggered by a transient CSS class
options.rationale: Add a `data-pulse` attribute or CSS class to the node wrapper when a WS update arrives, remove it after animation completes. Pure CSS @keyframes, no React re-render of the node needed — just a className toggle. Recommended because it's the lightest-weight approach with zero performance cost.

options.label: Update a 'lastUpdatedAt' field in node data and let GraphNode render a glow based on recency
options.rationale: More semantically meaningful — nodes that were recently updated glow brighter. But triggers React Flow node re-renders on every WS update which could be expensive with many nodes.

options.label: No visual indicator for individual updates (rely on data changes being visible in status/labels)
options.rationale: Simplest. Users see status changes reflected in the node. But loses the 'something just happened' affordance.

items.topic: How to handle 'Trigger Review' action for ExecutionRecords in the Flow lens
items.context: The spec lists 'Trigger Review' as an inspector action for ExecutionRecords in the Flow lens, but there's no existing API endpoint for triggering a review (only cancel, retry, follow-up exist). This either requires a new endpoint or a reinterpretation of the action.

options.label: Map 'Trigger Review' to updating execution status to 'needs_review' via PATCH
options.rationale: If there's a PATCH endpoint for execution records, setting status to 'needs_review' achieves the intent. Recommended because it uses existing update infrastructure without a dedicated endpoint.

options.label: Drop 'Trigger Review' from this item's scope — add it when a proper review workflow exists
options.rationale: Avoids a half-baked action. Review workflows may need more than a status change (notification, assignment, etc.). But reduces feature completeness.

items.freeform: I think it does already exist. Actually I am confident it does. It’s a git-control-tower integration. If it really doesn’t exist, then yes it needs an endpoint that communicates with git-control-tower using the ‘discovery’ package

items.topic: WebSocket reconnection: should full-fetch replace store or merge?
items.context: On WS reconnect, the plan calls for a full-fetch from the HTTP API before resuming the stream. The question is whether this full-fetch should replace the entire graph-data-store (like initial load) or merge with existing state. Replacing is simpler but causes a visual flash; merging preserves positions but risks stale nodes lingering.

options.label: Full replace (same as initial load) — call setGraphData() with fresh data
options.rationale: Simplest and most correct — guaranteed to match server state. The visual flash is acceptable because reconnection is an exceptional event. Dagre re-layout runs anyway on data change. Recommended for correctness.

options.label: Merge: add new nodes, update existing, remove absent ones
options.rationale: Smoother visual transition. Preserves user's mental map of node positions. But adds complexity and risk of stale state if merge logic has bugs.
